cross-013.answer: Skiff runs Tern at the Performance preset, which saves 1.8 ms over Quality (2.1 ms vs 3.9 ms); the premise about the lowest preset is true for Meridian (Ultra Performance), but Skiff does not use it. Record: dec-run-tern-on-skiff-at-the-performance-preset--74eqayfa83ybqpe3

cross-015.answer: Two Efforts are no longer active. The Shader compile cache and build farm Effort is completed: every farm build reads from the cache after dec-turn-the-shader-compile-cache-on-for-every-farm--4rr3b12b4sasdmaj (accepted 2026-03-20), which the retrospective fnd-retrospective-on-the-shader-compile-cache--9rpv2a60ach04cx6 confirms. The Co-op rollback netcode prototype Effort is abandoned: dec-abandon-rollback-netcode-for-co-op--46envrg0v4pdwv7b stopped rollback because re-running tides on each rolled-back frame costs 4.8 ms on Skiff, and co-op will not ship with rollback.

netcode-004.answer: The team abandoned rollback because re-running the tide simulation on every rolled-back frame costs 4.8 ms on Skiff, about a fifth of the 25 ms frame, while co-op needs bit-for-bit deterministic tides (dec-abandon-rollback-netcode-for-co-op--46envrg0v4pdwv7b). The reason depends on the world Decision "Run the tide simulation in 32.32 fixed point" (dec-run-the-tide-simulation-in-32-32-fixed-point--c5rjfcnmhne4h05e).

ports-012.answer: The ports team raised the Skiff dynamic resolution floor to 576p in dec-raise-the-skiff-dynamic-resolution-floor-to-576p--fep9q7m08pp9f0bb because 540p internal resolution made saltglass caustics shimmer badly in motion, even with Tern (fnd-saltglass-caustics-shimmer-at-the-540p-floor--0aa8sts89vhq1s6q). That decision was later superseded by a 504p floor.

ports-013.answer: Ship Tern as Lantern's only upscaler

render-031.answer: Alpha-tested foliage cost 2.1 ms in the visibility buffer versus 0.8 ms in forward+, so it was moved to a forward pass; saltglass was moved so it could refract the resolved scene (dec-visibility-buffer-for-opaque-geometry-foliage-an--gvnvp04jgm7kbfh9).

render-032.answer: Tern was chosen as Lantern's only upscaler because Halcyon has no Skiff build, and shipping it on two platforms would break the one-upscaler constraint; owning the code also mattered more than raw quality for saltglass, since its upscaler changes can be made in-house rather than through vendor tickets. See dec-ship-tern-as-lantern-s-only-upscaler--fmreq35nzyjc7k4e.

render-046.answer: The cost finding that had sunk virtual shadow maps was a capture error; with cached pages, VSM costs 1.4 ms, less than four cascades, and CSM still leaves unsolved cascade seams through saltglass (dec-use-virtual-shadow-maps-for-the-sun--x8nqkn9q7eaf1ap4, reopened 2026-01-12 after being rejected_by dec-use-cascaded-shadow-maps-with-four-cascades--s5c1y9jaf275afzr).

render-047.answer: It was a re-measurement: a release-build capture put the visibility buffer at 7.4 ms on Skiff against 8.1 ms for forward+ (6.3 ms with half-rate material resolve), so the forward+ fallback was no longer worth keeping. Record: dec-visibility-buffer-on-all-platforms-skiff-resolve--k1ackk3c3275r5y1

world-036.answer: Fibers were retired because 41% of alpha crash reports had no usable stack, which blocked crash triage for beta, and a continuation-wait prototype kept workers at 93% busy versus the 95% fibers gave, so the utilisation gain did not justify the unreadable crashes and Gull thread-local bug. Record: dec-return-engine-jobs-to-a-thread-pool-with-continu--1zkc1v2x97taf50h

world-051.answer: The team chose 32.32 fixed point because integer adds and multiplies give the same bits on every CPU and compiler, so the drift float tides showed between machines within 6 minutes cannot happen; the strict IEEE option was rejected in favor of it (dec-run-the-tide-simulation-in-32-32-fixed-point--c5rjfcnmhne4h05e).

world-055.answer: The cold-cache rerun's loss applied to Kelp's 4 MB dictionary, so the team shrank the dictionary to 1 MB (dec-shrink-kelp-s-dictionary-to-1-mb-for-streamed-as--yh8hktfqnyqhepew), where Kelp still beats Zstandard cold on Skiff: 1.5 GB/s vs 1.2 GB/s after firmware 3.2 (fnd-kelp-with-a-1-mb-dictionary-decodes-at-1-5-gb-s--y9v8jrxgbv6abrx5).
